reason: Section 58 requires annual work statements from mineral claim holders and allows statements to cover contiguous grouped claims.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Annual statement of mineral claim work
proposedGroups.reason: Section 58 requires annual work statements from mineral claim holders and allows statements to cover contiguous grouped claims.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the annual statement duty for mineral claim work and grouped contiguous claims.

reason: Section 58.1 covers grouping contiguous mineral claims, effects on dates fees and work, separation, cancellation, and group status.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration of contiguous mineral claim groups
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 58.1(1) allows holders to group two or more mineral claims by registry registration and fee payment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how contiguous mineral claims may be grouped.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Effects on registration date fees and required work
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 58.1(3) through 58.1(5) set the deemed date, renewal fee, and required work value by reference to the first registered claim.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how grouping affects registration dates, renewal fees, and required work.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Separation cancellation and group status
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 58.1(6) through 58.1(8) address separating units, cancellation or surrender, and when grouped status ends.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how mineral claim units may be separated and how cancellation or surrender affects grouped status.

reason: Section 59 allows the holder to surrender all or part of a mineral claim by registration in the registry.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Surrender of mineral claim by registration
proposedGroups.reason: Section 59 allows the holder to surrender all or part of a mineral claim by registration in the registry.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a holder may surrender a mineral claim or part of a claim.

reason: Section 60 separates post-expiry removal rights, Crown vesting and disposal, continuing liability, and withdrawal of claim area.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Removal of holder property after claim ends
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 60(1) allows the former holder six months to remove structures, equipment, machinery, or other property after expiry, surrender, or cancellation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the former holder's six-month removal right after a mineral claim ends.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown vesting and disposal of remaining property
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 60(2) vests remaining holder property in the Crown, subject to agreements, and allows Minister disposal.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when property remaining on a claim area vests in the Crown and may be disposed of.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuing liability after claim ends
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 60(3) keeps the former holder liable for obligations existing immediately before expiry, surrender, or cancellation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which obligations continue after a mineral claim ends.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Withdrawal of expired or surrendered claim area
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 60(4) withdraws the claim area after expiry or surrender for the period specified by the Recorder.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the withdrawal effect after expiry or surrender of a mineral claim.

reason: Section 61 covers notice of dispute filing, contents, service address, late filing limits, Recorder steps, and application of dispute provisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Filing notice of dispute over mineral claim registration
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 61(1) and 61(2) allow a prospector to file a duplicate notice of dispute with the prescribed fee.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may file a notice of dispute and what must accompany it.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Claimed entitlement and address for service
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 61(3) and 61(4) require particulars if entitlement is claimed and an address for service.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what entitlement details and service address are required in a notice of dispute.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Late filing limits and Recorder steps
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 61(5) and 61(6) limit filing after 60 days and require the Recorder to note, retain, mail, and send the notice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a late notice of dispute may be filed and what the Recorder must do after filing.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application of dispute provisions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 61(7) applies sections 13 and 113 after section 61 requirements are met.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which provisions apply once notice of dispute requirements are met.

reason: Section 62 allows regional surveys to be credited toward required work and sets fifteen-year and five-year report deadlines plus regulation compliance.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regional survey credits and reports
proposedGroups.reason: Section 62 allows regional surveys to be credited toward required work and sets fifteen-year and five-year report deadlines plus regulation compliance.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when regional surveys may be credited toward required work and when reports are due.

reason: Section 63 requires the person causing an airborne geological, geophysical, or geochemical survey for minerals to inform the Recorder before commencement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Prior notice of airborne survey
proposedGroups.reason: Section 63 requires the person causing an airborne geological, geophysical, or geochemical survey for minerals to inform the Recorder before commencement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the prior notice duty before airborne mineral surveys.

Section 65 prohibits abandoning, discarding, dumping, destroying, or otherwise reducing drill core or cuttings technical value without Recorder permission, subject to exceptions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Prohibition on reducing technical value of drill core or cuttings
proposedGroups.reason: Section 65 prohibits abandoning, discarding, dumping, destroying, or otherwise reducing drill core or cuttings technical value without Recorder permission, subject to exceptions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the prohibition on reducing the technical value of drill core or cuttings without permission.

reason: Section 66 requires notice before unauthorized reduction of drill core or cuttings value, lists Recorder response options, allocates Crown expense, and creates a six-month non-response exception.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice and Recorder actions for intended drill core disposal
proposedGroups.reason: Section 66 requires notice before unauthorized reduction of drill core or cuttings value, lists Recorder response options, allocates Crown expense, and creates a six-month non-response exception.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the notice, Recorder action, Crown expense, and six-month non-response rules for drill core or cuttings.

reason: Section 67 prohibits production unless the person is the holder of a mining lease.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease required for production

evidenceText: Prohibitions unless holder of mining lease

proposedGroups.reason: Section 67 prohibits production unless the person is the holder of a mining lease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that production may not be carried on unless the person holds a mining lease.

reason: Section 68 is a detailed mining lease grant provision that should be split into eligibility, application submissions, environmental approval, survey exception, and conversion effect.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Eligibility and necessity for mining lease application
proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs 68(1)(a), 68(1)(a.1), and 68(1)(b) require good-standing claims, whole claim units, mineral proof, and a production decision.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the claim status, land-unit, orebody, and production-decision conditions for obtaining a mining lease.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Required application submissions and security
proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs 68(1)(c) and 68(1)(d) require feasibility, corporate or partnership information, landowner or security proof, environmental security, mineral rights, fees, rent, and required work proof.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the information, proof, security, fee, rent, and required-work submissions for a mining lease application.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Environmental program approval before lease grant
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 68(2) bars grant until the Minister approves the protection, reclamation, and rehabilitation program after obtaining specified approvals.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the environmental program approval condition before granting a mining lease.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Boundary survey exception and mineral claim replacement
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 68(3) and 68(4) address when another boundary survey is not required and when mineral claims are replaced by the mining lease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the prior-survey exception and the effect of the first mining lease term on mineral claims.

reason: Section 69 sets duplicate execution, filing and recording, attorney instrument filing, and Recorder certification on the counterpart.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Execution filing recording and certification of mining leases
proposedGroups.reason: Section 69 sets duplicate execution, filing and recording, attorney instrument filing, and Recorder certification on the counterpart.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how mining leases are executed, filed, recorded, and certified.

reason: Section 70 requires annual rent by anniversary date and reduces coal mining lease rent by prior-year royalty while preserving a minimum.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease rent and coal royalty reduction
proposedGroups.reason: Section 70 requires annual rent by anniversary date and reduces coal mining lease rent by prior-year royalty while preserving a minimum.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall annual rent timing and the coal royalty reduction rule for mining leases.

reason: Section 71 requires annual work statements and reports when not in production and applies mineral claim renewal provisions to mining leases with modifications.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Annual mining lease work statement and report
proposedGroups.reason: Section 71 requires annual work statements and reports when not in production and applies mineral claim renewal provisions to mining leases with modifications.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall annual work statement and report duties for mining leases not in production.

reason: Section 72 sets the mining lease term at twenty years, subject to renewal.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Twenty-year mining lease term
proposedGroups.reason: Section 72 sets the mining lease term at twenty years, subject to renewal.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the basic duration of a mining lease.

reason: Section 73 allows renewal for a further twenty-year term on written application at least six months before expiry, with up to two additional twenty-year terms.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease renewal timing and additional terms
proposedGroups.reason: Section 73 allows renewal for a further twenty-year term on written application at least six months before expiry, with up to two additional twenty-year terms.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when and how a mining lease may be renewed.

reason: Section 74 prohibits assignment or transfer of lease rights without written Minister consent and allows refusal in the public interest.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister consent required for mining lease assignment or transfer
proposedGroups.reason: Section 74 prohibits assignment or transfer of lease rights without written Minister consent and allows refusal in the public interest.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the consent requirement and public-interest refusal rule for mining lease transfers.
